title: Epochal shadow trace with interruptible promotes and memory-safe rewind
author: Marina Kovács
ci_status: pass (flaky integration tests rerun twice; all green on final)
release_notes: Introduce epochal shadow tracing and a compact snapshot store to support deterministic counterfactual replays, interruptible promotes, and memory-safe rewind. Adds operator endpoints and console controls for pause/resume promotes.
description: Motivation: some rollouts require deterministic counterfactuals for postmortem/simulator fidelity and safe mid-promotion interrupts. Existing shadow capture was ephemeral and high-memory; promoting under pressure could lose replay fidelity and make automated rollback decisions brittle. This change introduces an 'epochal shadow trace' and accompanying compact snapshot store so shadowed requests can be replayed deterministically across promotion windows, and promotes can be interrupted and safely resumed or rolled back without requiring full reruns. Summary: adds a new epochal trace store that shards traces by epoch id and compacts KV/prefix material into delta snapshots; exposes a promote controller extension with interrupt/pause/resume APIs and a decision-simulator that runs counterfactuals against snapshots to produce rollback confidence scores. Also introduces a memory-safe rewind path that can reconstruct model-serving state at snapshot time without retaining full KV cache in memory. Commits: "add epochal trace store and compact snapshotter"; "interruptible promote controller + admin APIs"; "counterfactual replay simulator and rollback scorer"; "console: promote panel controls and telemetry"; "e2e and perf harness + docs". Files changed (high-level): server/rollouts/epochal_trace.go, server/rollouts/snapshot_store.go, server/rollouts/promote_controller.go, server/rollouts/replay_simulator.go, server/rollouts/kv_reconstructor.go, console/ui/promote_panel.tsx, docs/rollouts/epochal_trace.md, infra/e2e/epochal_trace_test.py, perf/bench/trace_memory.bench, ci/workflows/rollouts.yml. Design notes: epoch boundaries are user-configurable and aligned with canary windows; traces are indexed by (epoch_id, cohort_id, trace_hash) and stored on fast object storage with a compact delta format to bound memory. The promote controller supports an interrupt token; when interrupted the controller snapshots current epoch state, halts traffic promotion, and runs the replay simulator as a background job to produce a deterministic rollback score. The memory-safe rewind path reconstructs minimal KV state on demand using snapshot deltas and a deterministic apply-order so that counters and caches match previous execution without holding the full KV cache. Tests & perf: added unit tests for snapshot compaction, deterministic replay determinism, and promote interrupt/resume semantics; e2e harness runs a synthetic cohort with shadowing across 50k requests to validate fidelity; perf benches show snapshot store reduces peak memory by ~7x versus naive capture in our internal cluster. Review and iteration: initial review called out potential stall where replay simulator could block autoscaler decisions; I added asynchronous replay with bounded CPU quota and a prioritization hook so SRE can throttle simulator jobs during peak traffic. Reviewer notes included a request to make epoch retention configurable per-tenant (done) and to expose conservative fallback behavior when snapshot reconstruct fails (added fallback to fail-closed and opt-in fail-open via tenant policy). Conversation summary: Priya: "Nice separation of concerns; ensure tenant quotas limit trace store growth." Author reply: "added per-tenant retention and compact-on-write policy, documented tradeoffs." Diego: "What happens with long-lived sessions spanning epochs?" Author reply: "we attach session anchors to traces and the KV reconstructor stitches anchors across snapshots; added tests for 0->1->2 epoch transitions." Sophie: "CI flaked on integration test due to timing; reran and added retries to harness." CI summary: initial run had two flaky integration failures unrelated to core algorithm (test harness timing); reran workflows/rollouts.yml twice and all checks passed. Merge notes: squashed into a single commit, added release notes, and documented operator runbook with abort/retry playbook under docs/runbooks/rollouts-epochal.md. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers, start with 0.5% shadow seeding for one week, increase to 5% with replay checks, then enable interruptible promotes for select tenants. Observability: new metrics: rollout.epoch.trace.size, rollout.epoch.replay.latency, rollout.promote.interrupts, rollout.replay.rollback_score; added dashboard templates and alerts for unexpected trace-store growth. Backwards compatibility: new endpoints are admin-only and feature-flagged; no customer-facing API changes. Follow-ups: integrate with Optimize recommendations to suggest epoch sizing for workloads and add a dry-run-only mode in the console for non-destructive counterfactual scoring.
